questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
Groups helping Republicans have spent $495K in the MS Senate race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is defense.

questions.prompt: A party's coordinated spending in the last three weeks before Nov. 3 is disclosed when?
questions.why: Coordinated spending appears only on regular reports. Anything after Oct. 14 lands on the post-general report, due Dec. 3.

questions.prompt: After NRSC v. FEC (June 2026), how much can a party spend in coordination with its Senate nominee?
options: Up to a set limit per state
questions.why: The Supreme Court struck down the limits on party coordinated spending, so parties can now spend without limit alongside their candidates.

questions.prompt: What starts the clock on a 24- or 48-hour spending report?
questions.why: The reporting clock starts on the dissemination date, when the ad first reaches the public.
